newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY -- A High Court judge ruled the Democratic Party could not challenge the provisional legislature in court and said the judiciary must not be used to settle political battles.

-- MING PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin will arrive in Shenzhen on June 28 to join other members of China's handover delegation. Vice-minister of public security Tian Qiyu has been travelling between Hong Kong and China to ensure security during the handover ceremony.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sources said Chinese regulators met several red chip companies last week. It intends to suggest all asset injections of red chips be approved and handled by a national assets management bureau under the Ministry of Finance.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Chinese government will issue instructions soon to limit government officials' participation in overseas promotional activities by red chip companies.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- A Chinese official said Xinhua News Agency will have four new functions after the handover including collecting intelligence, promoting Chinese policies in the territory, introducing Hong Kong's experiences to the mainland to help its economic reforms, and co-ordinating Hong Kong people getting involved in political activities on the mainland.

-- WEN WEI PO -- After eight years of rapid development, China's assests evaluation business is nearing international standards, with more than 3,300 assests evaluation organisations by the end of 1996 employing more than 50,000 staff.

-- SING TAO -- As the British army needs several hours after the handover to depart Hong Kong, so China is demanding that the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong Garrison arrive in the territory before midnight of June 30.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Sources said Beijing's plans to regulate Hong Kong-listed red chips are expected to make initial public offerings by mainland firms the main target.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Three highly respected judges were welcomed as a dream team who would give the future Court of Final Appeal the credibility needed to maintain international confidence in Hong Kong.
